lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner responds to the open prompt 'Describe a time you faced a challenge and what you learned from handling it' by either drawing on their own real experience or by writing as the provided fictional narrator, Sam, who is preparing a personal statement for a program Sam is applying to.
safetyNotes: The learner may write about a real experience only if they choose to, and only details they are comfortable sharing; using the provided fictional narrator, Sam, instead is a fully equal option and is never treated as a lesser response.
No one but the learner (and anyone the learner chooses to share it with) needs to read the finished statement; scoring looks only at craft, not at the truth or quality of the underlying life event.
materials: learner-local: the provided fictional narrator prompt (Sam) as an optional alternative

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What is one sentence in your draft you're proudest of, and what makes it work better than a more generic version would have?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Opening specificity: Opening paragraph begins with a specific moment, action, or detail that grounds the reader in the scene. | Reflective depth: Statement names a lesson and gives one concrete example of it changing a later choice or action. | Craft awareness: Reflection names a sentence and gives a real reason grounded in craft (specificity, sensory detail, structure) for why it works. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a second, contrasting opening paragraph for the same statement that starts with dialogue instead of action or description, then compare which version is more effective and explain why in two or three sentences.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

resources.title: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner responds to the open prompt 'Describe a time you faced a challenge and what you learned from handling it' by either drawing on their own real experience or by writing as the provided fictional narrator, Sam, who is preparing a personal statement for a program Sam is applying to.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice decision or action.
Model move 2: Before drafting, decide whether you'll write about yourself or as the fictional narrator Sam, and jot the challenge you'll write about either way.
Model move 3: Draft an opening paragraph that pulls the reader into a specific moment, rather than starting with a general statement.

Model check: Opening specificity: Opening paragraph begins with a specific moment, action, or detail that grounds the reader in the scene. | Reflective depth: Statement names a lesson and gives one concrete example of it changing a later choice or action. | Craft awareness: Reflection names a sentence and gives a real reason grounded in craft (specificity, sensory detail, structure) for why it works.

resources.title: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner responds to the open prompt 'Describe a time you faced a challenge and what you learned from handling it' by either drawing on their own real experience or by writing as the provided fictional narrator, Sam, who is preparing a personal statement for a program Sam is applying to.
Coach direction: Before drafting, decide whether you'll write about yourself or as the fictional narrator Sam, and jot the challenge you'll write about either way.
Learner prompt: Which option are you choosing for this personal statement?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Draft an opening paragraph that pulls the reader into a specific moment, rather than starting with a general statement.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Write an opening paragraph (3-5 sentences) that puts the reader inside one specific moment of the challenge, rather than summarizing the whole situation in general terms.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My opening paragraph starts with a specific moment or detail, not a general statement like 'Throughout my life I have faced many challenges.'
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is one sentence in your draft you're proudest of, and what makes it work better than a more generic version would have?

Success checks: Opening specificity: Opening paragraph begins with a specific moment, action, or detail that grounds the reader in the scene. | Reflective depth: Statement names a lesson and gives one concrete example of it changing a later choice or action. | Craft awareness: Reflection names a sentence and gives a real reason grounded in craft (specificity, sensory detail, structure) for why it works.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Opening specificity: Opening paragraph begins with a specific moment, action, or detail that grounds the reader in the scene. | Reflective depth: Statement names a lesson and gives one concrete example of it changing a later choice or action. | Craft awareness: Reflection names a sentence and gives a real reason grounded in craft (specificity, sensory detail, structure) for why it works..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the writing a personal statement in the learner's own voice task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: What is one sentence in your draft you're proudest of, and what makes it work better than a more generic version would have?

Reflective depth: Statement names a lesson and gives one concrete example of it changing a later choice or action.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Opening specificity: Opening paragraph begins with a specific moment, action, or detail that grounds the reader in the scene. | Reflective depth: Statement names a lesson and gives one concrete example of it changing a later choice or action. | Craft awareness: Reflection names a sentence and gives a real reason grounded in craft (specificity, sensory detail, structure) for why it works.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u02-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
